state.what_it_does: A front end sends an id as an invoke header; the shell validates it (1-64 chars of letters, digits, _ : -) and enters it in a thread-local scope; the sink writes the scope id on every record the thread writes; the control client puts it in the request id as req.<n>.<id>, the control server and the asset-plane server read it, validate it, enter it for the request or connection and leave it again. A bad id is replaced by a minted one.

invalid_text_reaches_log.instructions: Can text that is not a valid id (a line break, a quote, a token, an over-long string) from the front end, the control envelope or the asset-plane header reach a log line as an id?

criteria.true: Yes, a path writes an unvalidated id.
criteria.false: No, every path validates before writing.

scope_leaks.instructions: Can one request's id remain in the thread-local scope after its request or connection has ended, so that a later request on the same thread is logged under it?

criteria.true: Yes, a scope can leak to a later request.
criteria.false: No, scopes are restored when the request or connection ends.

asset_connection_scope.instructions: Is the asset-plane id, taken from the first frame of a connection, entered for the right span: the whole connection, and not entered again or left entered by a later frame?

compat_old_peer.instructions: Can a peer that sends the old request id (req.<n>, no id) or an old asset-plane header (no corr member) still be served unchanged?

criteria.false: No, an old peer would break.

defect.instructions: Does this code contain a defect that should be fixed before committing?

criteria.true: Yes, a defect should be fixed.
